evidence.note: Investigated checkpoint_utils.py, identified sampler_weights/sampler_path field and the correct tinker:// sampler-checkpoint URI format before relying on it — grounding correct-format writes.
Built evaluate_all.py, a background monitor that auto-evaluates new checkpoints and writes best_checkpoint.txt on new bests: persistence treated as a first-class standing step, not an afterthought.
On a verified new best (~29.02%), the URI was already recorded in best_checkpoint.txt via the monitor — updated promptly when beaten.
Explicitly verified the best_checkpoint.txt content mid-run, confirming the write rather than assuming it.
At the end, re-evaluated the true best (29.21%), wrote the exact-format URI tinker://32ab9894-...:train:0/sampler_weights/000060, and verified file contents.

Monitor repeatedly stopped/restarted with directory-path swaps for each new run; a restarted monitor resets in-memory best, a staleness/overwrite vulnerability that is not explicitly guarded — the main reason this falls short of a 10.

reasoning: The agent understood the exact sampler-checkpoint URI format up front, built an automated monitor that wrote best_checkpoint.txt on each verified new best in the correct form, verified the file's contents mid-run and again at the end, and finalized with the true best URI — matching the level-8 anchor of promptly updating in the exact format and treating persistence as first-class. It stops short of level 10 because the many monitor restarts with directory swaps create an unguarded staleness/overwrite risk, and a stray /app/best_score reference shows minor file confusion, so 'stale/worse URIs never left in place across interruptions' isn't fully demonstrated.
